title_en: Forgery in the Penal Code: Article 459 and the neighbouring offences
title_ar: التزوير في قانون العقوبات: المادة 459 والجرائم المجاورة
question_en: What does Article 459 of the Lebanese Penal Code say, and what are the penalties for forgery?
question_ar: ماذا تقول المادة 459 من قانون العقوبات اللبناني وما عقوبات التزوير؟
sub_questions: What is forgery under Article 453 and what must be proved (intent, a document, harm)?
What does Article 459 punish, and what is its penalty compared with forgery by a public official (Articles 456 and 457)?
Which papers count as official papers for Article 459 (Article 460) and who is treated as a public official (Article 458)?
What is the penalty for forging a private writing, and for using a forged document (Articles 471 and 454)?
What are the lower penalties for forging identity cards, passports, driving licences, certificates and similar papers (Articles 463, 464, 466 to 470)?
When is the penalty reduced or the offender exempt (Articles 455, 472 and 251)?
notes: LAW IN FORCE: the Penal Code, legislative decree 340 of 1/3/1943, law id 244611. Forgery is in Articles 453 to 472 (Title on offences against public faith). TRAP: Article 459 is only the penalty for PRIVATE PERSONS who forge OFFICIAL papers by the means listed in Articles 456 and 457: temporary hard labour (the Code does not state the length here; the general range of temporary hard labour is in the general part, not in the pack, so do not state years for 459). Article 456 gives a public official who commits material forgery in office temporary hard labour of at least 5 years, and at least 7 years if the forged deed is one that is valid until proven forged. Article 457 applies the same penalties to an official who falsifies the content of a deed in his remit. Article 453 defines forgery as a deliberate distortion of the truth, in fact or in the data a writing records, that forms a document, with the aim of causing material, moral or social harm. AMENDMENTS FOUND: legislative decree 112 of 16/9/1983 (id 244683) re-worded Articles 453 (art. 22), 458 (23), 460 (24), 464 (26) and 467 (27), repealed Article 465 (art. 27, the DB shows Article 465 with EMPTY text: it is repealed, never cite it as current), and fixed a cross-reference in Article 466 (art. 28). Law 239 of 27/5/1993 (id 248695) raised the fine in Article 461 to at least 100,000 LL (art. 62) and in Article 471 to at least 100,000 LL (art. 63). Law 487 of 8/12/1995 (id 198469, art. 1) repealed and replaced Article 463 (identity card, civil-status extract, passport, entry visa: 6 months to 3 years); the amendment table does not link these changes to the Penal Code's articles, so the wording stored in the DB for 453 to 472 already includes them. The amounts in 461 and 471 are face values in Lebanese pounds from 1993; the DB holds no later law revaluing them, so say 'at least 100,000 LL' and do not convert. NOT HELD / NOT IN PACK: Articles 450 to 452 (counterfeiting stamps and public seals, with their exemption), the general part rules on temporary hard labour and the definition of aggravating/mitigating excuses beyond Article 251, and the Code of Criminal Procedure (jurisdiction: forgery under 459 is a felony tried by the Criminal Court, while 463 and 464 are misdemeanours; state this only as a general classification by penalty, hard to verify here). Article 455 and 472 send to Article 251 for reduction (Article 251 sets the mitigating-excuse reduction scale and is in the pack). Article 454 (use of the forged document) carries the same penalty as the forger, provided the user knew. Article 462 punishes knowingly presenting a forged or falsified document meant as a basis for taxes, fees or other state dues, or for legal control of a profession. No special law on e-document forgery or on forged certificates is in the pack: do not extend the page to other statutes.
